# dsh-glm-web-search
Use your Z.AI (GLM) subscription as DeepSeek Harness's search, fetch and vision backend.
Sign in with the Z.AI account you already have — no API key, no separate billing.

GitHub ·

## Why this exists

DeepSeek Harness ships its own `web_search` / `web_fetch` backends, which means another API key
and

another bill. But plenty of people already pay for a Z.AI plan — and that quota can already
run `web
_search_prime` and `webReader` server-side. Nobody had wired it up.

This plugin does exactly that. **One email login turns your existing subscription into the
harness's

search and fetch capability.** Installing it is enough; the tool names and arguments
the model sees
do not change, only the service behind them.
## Features
| Capability | What it does |

| **Web search** | Replaces the official `web_search` backend with `web_search_prime` |
| **Web read

er** | Replaces the official `web_fetch` backend with `webReader` |
| **Vision** | Adds a `zai_visio

n` tool for image description, OCR and visual Q&A; |
| **Zero dependencies** | No `node_modules`, no

`dependencies`, no `peerDependencies` |
| **Status line** | `/dsh-glm-status` shows token age, plan
expiry and remaining quota |

## Configuration
| Field | Default | Purpose |

| `origin` | `https://zcode.z.ai` | Gateway origin |
| `model` | unset (resolved live) | Model that

runs search and fetch |
| `appVersion` | probed | Client version advertised to the gateway |
| `jwtE

nv` | `ZAI_JWT` | Credential reference |
| `tokenPath` | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-glm-web-search/token.json` |

Local token file |
| `vision` | `true` | Register the `zai_vision` tool |
| `timeoutMs` | `90000` |
Per-request deadline |

Credential order: managed record → `$ZAI_JWT` → the local token file.
On a headless host, set `ZAI_B
ROWSER_OPEN=0`; the URL is still printed so you can open it yourself.
## Two things worth knowing

**Search results are capped.** Upstream returns at most 10 sources per `web_search` call, and the
ha

rness's `dsh-tool-web` then truncates `sources[]` to **8** (setting `truncated: true`). One call
may
carry up to 4 queries, run concurrently; the merged result still hits the 8-source cap.

**It has no dependency tree at all.** `src/` reaches the harness only through injected services
(`ct

x.web`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.commands`), and imports nothing outside its own tree except Node
builtins

— so there is no `node_modules`, no `dependencies`, and no `peerDependencies`. That matters
beyond t

idiness: declaring a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer makes the harness's install preflight compare
your ra
nge against the runtime version and **reject the whole installation** when they disagree.

The subtler hazard is a second copy of a stateful harness package. Same version, byte-identical
file

s, and it still breaks: two files mean two *module instances*, and a module-local
`Symbol()` differs

between them. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` keys its internal scheduler on exactly
that (`const TOOL_RUN

TIME_SCHEDULER = Symbol("@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler")`), so
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` reac

hing through `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` finds
`undefined` and the turn dies with `Cannot re

ad properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`.
`Symbol.for()` keys live in a global registry and s

urvive duplication — `schemastery` uses one,
which is why it is safe to appear twice and `dsh-tools`

uplication — `schemastery` uses one,
which is why it is safe to appear twice and `dsh-tools` is not.

## FAQ

**Do I need a paid Z.AI plan?**
No. A free account gets an experience plan that already covers searc

h and fetch. Vision needs the
Flash model, which the same plan includes.

**Where is my credential stored?**
`$DSH_HOME/dsh-glm-web-search/token.json` — one file, no environm

ent variables required. Delete it
or run `logout` to revoke locally.

**Why do I only get 8 results?**
That is the harness's own cap, not Z.AI's. Upstream returns 10; `ds
